mainTopic: How many immersions (טבילות) and sanctifications (קידושין) the כהן גדול performs on יום כיפור, and why one פסוק in the יום כיפור פרשה is out of order
overview: This amud is about how many times the כהן גדול immerses (טבילה) and washes his hands and feet (קידוש) on יום כיפור. It opens by showing that both רבי מאיר and רבנן reach ten קידושין. רבנן place the last one at the end of the day, when he takes off the holy garments. A ברייתא then teaches that the פסוק 'ובא אהרן אל אהל מועד' is the only verse in the פרשה written out of order. It describes going back in to take out the כף and מחתה, and that happens only after the rams. רב חסדא explains why: there is a tradition of five טבילות, and the written order would give only three. רבי יהודה and רבי each bring a פסוק teaching that every switch from one service to another needs a טבילה. The ברייתא lists the five services, which alternate gold, white, gold, white, gold. Next it learns that each טבילה has two קידושין, one when undressing and one when dressing. This is shown from the פסוקים, from a קל וחומר, and from the extra words 'אשר לבש'. Finally the גמרא returns to רבי יהודה's source and asks how we know that switching from gold back to white also needs a טבילה, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's count ends at ten sanctifications
steps.stepSummary: This amud opens with the last words of רבי מאיר's count: ten קידושין in total.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a count that started on the previous page. According to רבי מאיר, the כהן גדול does ten קידושין of hands and feet on יום כיפור. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, each of the five טבילות comes with two קידושין, so five times two gives ten. That tidy total is what the next step questions for רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten sanctifications (washings of hands and feet)
Washing the hands and feet from the כיור before or after service

phrases.english: Ten sanctifications.
phrases.notes: The tail end of רבי מאיר's count from the previous page.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי מאיר's count from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר there are ten קידושין: two with each of the five טבילות.

steps.title: According to רבנן there are only nine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: according to רבנן, the count comes out to only nine קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבנן, there are only nine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem. The tradition says ten קידושין, but רבנן's method of counting seems to give only nine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן do not require an extra קידוש at the first טבילה, when the כהן גדול is still changing out of his regular clothes. That removes one, leaving nine. If everyone agrees there are ten, רבנן need to explain where the tenth comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: But / however. It signals a challenge.
According to the Rabbis (the חכמים who disagree with רבי מאיר)
There are only nine

phrases.english: But according to the Rabbis, there are nine!
phrases.notes: For רבנן the first טבילה has only one קידוש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבנן can reach the total of ten that רבי מאיר reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבנן's ability to arrive at ten קידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since רבנן drop one קידוש at the first טבילה, their total appears to be nine, not the traditional ten.

steps.title: רבנן place the last sanctification at the end of the day
steps.stepSummary: רבנן answer that the tenth קידוש is done at the very end, when the כהן גדול takes off the holy garments and puts on his own clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן can say to you: the final sanctification, when he takes off the holy garments and puts on regular clothes, he does it there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers on behalf of רבנן. The missing tenth קידוש happens at the end of the day, when the כהן גדול changes back into his own clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן lose one קידוש at the start of the day but gain one at the end. When the service is over and he removes the בגדי קודש, he washes his hands and feet there. So רבנן also reach ten, just distributed differently from רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: They can say to you (introduces a defense)
The last sanctification
Holy (priestly) garments
Regular, non-holy clothes
There, at that point

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי מאיר and רבנן count ten קידושין. They disagree about where they fall: רבנן add one at the very end of the day, when he takes off the holy garments.

phrases.english: The Rabbis can say to you:
The final sanctification,
when he takes off the holy garments
and puts on regular clothes,
he performs it there.
phrases.notes: The tenth קידוש is added at the end of the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by locating רבנן's tenth קידוש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocation: the missing item is found at a different point in the day
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבנן have only nine קידושין because the first טבילה lacks one.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן add a קידוש at the end, when he removes the holy garments, which brings the total to ten.

steps.title: One verse in the יום כיפור passage is out of order
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that 'ובא אהרן אל אהל מועד' describes going in to remove the כף and מחתה, and that this is the only verse in the פרשה not written in order.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: 'And אהרן shall come into the אהל מועד.' Why does he come? Only to take out the spoon and the coal pan. The whole passage was written in order except for this verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a פסוק in the יום כיפור service. It says this verse describes the כהן גדול going back in to remove the כף and the מחתה, and that this verse is out of order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this point the inner service is already finished, so why does אהרן go back in? The ברייתא answers that he goes in to retrieve the vessels he left in the קודש הקדשים. In real practice this happens later, after the rams that appear in the next verse, so this one verse is out of sequence.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tent of Meeting (here, the inner Sanctuary)
The spoon that held the incense
The coal pan
In order (the actual sequence of the service)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the תורה's verses always match the real order of the יום כיפור service. This ברייתא says one specific verse (16:23) actually happens after the next verse (16:24).

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And Aaron shall come into the Tent of Meeting"
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from ויקרא טז:כג.

phrases.english: Why does he come?
He comes only to take out
the spoon and the coal pan.
For the entire passage
was stated in order,
except for this verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וּבָא אַהֲרֹן אֶל אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the sequence of verses in the יום כיפור פרשה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ובא אהרן' refers to removing the כף and מחתה, and it is the only verse in the פרשה written out of order.

steps.title: Why is this verse out of order?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason this one verse is out of sequence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we must say this verse is out of order. This short question sets up רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we read verses in their written order. Claiming that one verse is displaced needs a reason, and the גמרא is asking what forces this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the ברייתא's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why must 'ובא אהרן' be read as out of order rather than as written?

steps.title: רב חסדא: the tradition of five immersions requires it
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that there is a tradition of five טבילות and ten קידושין, but the written order would give only three טבילות and six קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: We have a tradition that the כהן גדול immerses five times and sanctifies ten times on this day. If the service followed the written order, you would find only three immersions and six sanctifications.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. A received tradition says five טבילות, and only reading this verse as displaced produces that number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read in written order, the כהן גדול would remove the כף and מחתה right away and then change once for the rams, which gives only three טבילות. In the true order, he goes out to do the rams, then goes back in to remove the vessels, then comes out again. Those extra trips in and out add two more changes of clothes, making five טבילות.

keyTerms.meaning: We have learned as a tradition
Immersions in a מקוה
The High Priest
In their (written) order
You would not find

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a received tradition about practice can determine how we read the order of verses in the תורה.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: We have learned as a tradition,
five immersions and ten sanctifications

phrases.aramaic: טוֹבֵל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם.
phrases.english: the High Priest immerses and sanctifies on that day.
And if done in their written order,
you would not find them,
only three immersions and six sanctifications.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason requested in the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tradition of five טבילות can only be met if the vessels are removed after the rams. That is why the verse must be out of order.

steps.title: רבי יהודה derives the five immersions from the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה shows from the פסוק itself that the כהן גדול immerses when moving from one service to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה said: From where do we know the five immersions and ten sanctifications of the כהן גדול on this day? The verse says: 'And אהרן shall come into the אהל מועד, take off the linen garments, wash his flesh in water in a holy place, put on his garments, go out and perform.'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings a scriptural source for the five טבילות. רבי יהודה points to the verse describing a change of clothes between services.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the verse, the כהן גדול takes off the linen garments, washes his body, dresses again, and then goes out to serve. So moving from the inner service to the outer service requires a טבילה. Here the number five comes from the פסוק, not only from tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
The verse teaches
The linen (white) garments
And he shall wash his flesh (immersion)

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
From where do we know the five immersions and ten sanctifications

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁטּוֹבֵל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם?
phrases.english: that the High Priest immerses and sanctifies on that day?
The verse teaches:
"And Aaron shall come into the Tent of Meeting
and take off the linen garments
and wash his flesh in water in a holy place
and put on his garments
and go out and perform."
phrases.notes: These words come from ויקרא טז:כג-כד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a scriptural source for the five טבילות that רב חסדא based on tradition.
steps.raayaObject: The five טבילות and ten קידושין of the כהן גדול
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא טז:כג-כד: the verse describes washing and changing clothes between the inner service and the outer service.

steps.title: Every switch between services requires immersion
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה concludes: anyone who moves from one service to another needs a טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From this you learn that anyone who switches from one service to another requires immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה draws the general rule from the verse. Every change from one type of service to another needs a טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each switch between the white-garment service and the gold-garment service on יום כיפור requires a טבילה. Counting every switch through the day gives five טבילות, each with two קידושין, for ten in total.

keyTerms.meaning: From this you learn
One who switches from one service to another
Requires immersion

steps.whatToRemember: On יום כיפור, every switch between the inner (white) service and the outer (gold) service requires a טבילה. That makes five טבילות and ten קידושין, and it explains why removing the כף and מחתה happens after the rams.

phrases.english: From this you learn
that anyone who switches from one service to another
requires immersion.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָמַדְתָּ שֶׁכׇּל הַמְשַׁנֶּה מֵעֲבוֹדָה לַעֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the general principle drawn from the verse quoted in the previous step.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Every switch between services requires a טבילה, which produces the five טבילות of יום כיפור.

steps.title: רבי learns the immersions from the verse about the linen garments
steps.stepSummary: רבי derives the five טבילות and ten קידושין from ויקרא ט״ז:ד. He concludes that anyone who switches from one service to another needs a טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: Where do we learn the five immersions and ten hand-and-foot washings that the כהן גדול does on יום כיפור? From the פסוק: 'He shall wear a holy linen tunic, linen pants on his flesh, a linen belt and a linen turban. They are holy garments, and he shall wash his flesh in water and put them on.' This teaches that whoever switches from one service to another must immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא, רבי, gives his own פסוק as the source for the five immersions. It is the פסוק about putting on the white linen clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה (step 7) learned the rule from the פסוקים at the end of the service. רבי uses the earlier פסוק, where the תורה says to wash and then put on the linen clothes. Since changing into the special clothes requires washing, each switch between services requires a טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Full-body immersion in a מקוה
Washing the hands and feet from the כיור (the Temple washbasin)
One who switches from one type of service to another
The linen garments (the white clothes)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up טבילה and קידוש. טבילה means immersing the whole body. קידוש means washing only the hands and feet. The day has five of the first and ten of the second.

phrases.english: Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) said:
From where do we learn the five immersions and ten sanctifications

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁטּוֹבֵל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם,
phrases.english: that the High Priest immerses and sanctifies on that day?
As it says: "A holy linen tunic he shall wear,
and linen pants shall be on his flesh,
and with a linen belt he shall gird himself,
and with a linen turban he shall wrap his head;
they are holy garments,
and he shall wash his flesh in water and put them on."

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָמַדְתָּ שֶׁכׇּל הַמְשַׁנֶּה מֵעֲבוֹדָה לַעֲבוֹדָה —
phrases.english: So you have learned that anyone who switches from one service to another
requires immersion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: מִנַּיִן לְחָמֵשׁ טְבִילוֹת וַעֲשָׂרָה קִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, parallel source for the same rule רבי יהודה just concluded
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From ויקרא ט״ז:ד we learn that every switch from one service to another requires a טבילה.

steps.title: The words 'they are holy garments' compare all the garments
steps.stepSummary: The words 'בגדי קדש הם' link all the garments together. So the gold garments, and not only the white ones, also need a טבילה when the כהן גדול puts them on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסוק says 'they are holy garments.' This compares all the garments to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי adds a support from the words 'they are holy garments.' These words show that the rule applies to every set of clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself only talks about the white linen clothes. Through a הקש, the gold clothes are treated the same way. So changing into the gold clothes also requires a טבילה, and that is how we reach a total of five.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it says': introduces an additional פסוק as support
They were compared; a הקש is a comparison the Torah makes, so a law in one case applies to the other
The gold garments, which the כהן גדול wears all year

phrases.english: And it says: "they are holy garments";

phrases.aramaic: הוּקְשׁוּ כׇּל הַבְּגָדִים כּוּלָּן זֶה לָזֶה.
phrases.english: all the garments, every one of them, are compared to one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule from the white garments to the gold garments
steps.raayaObject: That the gold garments also require טבילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The phrase בגדי קדש הם, read as a הקש between all the garments

steps.title: The five services of יום כיפור and their clothes
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the five services of the day. They alternate between gold and white clothes, which explains why there are five טבילות.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are five services: the morning תמיד in gold clothes; the special service of the day in white clothes; his ram and the people's ram in gold clothes; taking out the spoon and coal pan in white clothes; and the afternoon תמיד in gold clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists the five services in order, along with the clothes for each one. This shows where the five טבילות come from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is gold, white, gold, white, gold. Each service begins with a טבילה, so five services give five טבילות. Two קידושין come with each טבילה, which gives the ten קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily morning offering
The special יום כיפור service (the bull, the goats, the incense)
His own ram and the ram of the people (עולות)
The incense spoon and the coal pan, taken out of the קודש הקדשים
The daily afternoon offering

steps.whatToRemember: Gold, white, gold, white, gold: five services, so five טבילות and ten קידושין.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice that taking out the כף and מחתה comes after the rams. That is why, back in step 4, the פסוק 'ובא אהרן' was called out of order.

phrases.english: And they are five services:
the morning daily offering, in gold garments;
the service of the day, in white garments;
his ram and the people's ram, in gold garments;
the spoon and coal pan, in white garments;

phrases.aramaic: תָּמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם בְּבִגְדֵי זָהָב.
phrases.english: the afternoon daily offering, in gold garments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the five services that produce the five טבילות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The day has five services that alternate gold-white-gold-white-gold, and each requires a טבילה.

steps.title: Why does each immersion need two washings?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source that every טבילה comes with two קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where do we learn that each immersion needs two hand-and-foot washings?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא has explained the five טבילות. Now it asks how we get to ten קידושין. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five טבילות give us ten קידושין only if each טבילה has two washings. The ברייתא wants a source for that specific point.

keyTerms.meaning: Each and every immersion
Two washings of the hands and feet

phrases.english: And from where do we learn that each and every immersion
requires two sanctifications?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁכׇּל טְבִילָה וּטְבִילָה צְרִיכָה שְׁנֵי קִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the five טבילות to the ten קידושין
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that each טבילה is paired with two קידושין

steps.title: One washing when undressing, one when dressing
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוקים 'ופשט... ורחץ' and 'ורחץ... ולבש' we learn that there is a קידוש when taking off the clothes and another when putting on the new ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'He shall take off... and wash,' and 'he shall wash... and put on.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by pointing to the פסוקים. One washing is linked to taking off the clothes, and another is linked to putting on the new clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah connects 'washing' both to undressing (ופשט ורחץ) and to dressing (ורחץ ולבש). So a קידוש comes before the טבילה, after taking off the old clothes. Another קידוש comes after the טבילה, when putting on the new clothes. Two per טבילה, times five, equals ten.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches': introduces the פסוק that answers the question
And he shall take off (the clothes)
And he shall put on (the clothes)

steps.whatToRemember: Every טבילה has a קידוש before it (after undressing) and a קידוש after it (when dressing).

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And he shall take off... and he shall wash,"
"and he shall wash... and put on."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוקים link a washing to undressing and a washing to dressing, which makes two קידושין per טבילה

steps.title: A קל וחומר for the washings
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון learns the need for קידוש from a קל וחומר. If an ordinary entry into the service needs קידוש without טבילה, then a case that requires טבילה surely needs קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says it is a קל וחומר: in a place where no immersion is required, washing the hands and feet is still required. So in a place where immersion is required, isn't it logical that washing is required too?
steps.whatsHappening: A different תנא gives a second way to learn the קידוש rule. He uses logic (a קל וחומר) instead of the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every regular כהן must wash his hands and feet before the service, even though he does not need to immerse. On יום כיפור the כהן גדול's changes are more serious, since they require full טבילה. It would be strange for them not to require the lesser washing as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a more serious one
Is it not logical? (the conclusion of a קל וחומר)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the קידושין can be learned either from the פסוקים or from logic. The very next step asks how many קידושין this קל וחומר actually proves.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, קַל וָחוֹמֶר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says: it is learned by a kal vachomer:
Just as in a place that does not require immersion,
sanctification is required,
then in a place that does require immersion,
is it not logical that sanctification is required?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a logical source in place of the scriptural one in step 13
steps.raayaObject: That the טבילות of יום כיפור require קידוש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the ordinary daily service, where קידוש is required without טבילה

steps.title: Maybe the logic only gives one sanctification
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges its own קל וחומר. Maybe it only proves one קידוש per change of clothes, like the ordinary case it came from.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps: just as there (an ordinary entry into the עבודה) there is only one קידוש, so too here (on יום כיפור) there should be only one קידוש?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible objection to the קל וחומר from step 14. It warns that the קל וחומר may only teach one קידוש, not two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר cannot teach more than the case it is learned from. The ordinary case has only one קידוש, so the קל וחומר might only give one קידוש here too. That would not explain the two קידושין for every טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: If, just as there… (opens a comparison that might limit the law)
One washing of the hands and feet

steps.confusionAlert: 'להלן' (there) is NOT another יום כיפור case. It is the ordinary daily entry into the עבודה, which needs only one קידוש.

phrases.english: If: just as there, one sanctification,
phrases.notes: 'There' means an ordinary entry into the service, which is where the קל וחומר comes from.

phrases.english: so too here, one sanctification?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן קִידּוּשׁ אֶחָד, אַף כָּאן קִידּוּשׁ אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the קל וחומר of step 14 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A derived law cannot be stronger than its source. The source has only one קידוש, so the קל וחומר cannot produce two.

steps.title: 'That he put on' compares removing clothes to putting them on
steps.stepSummary: The extra words 'אשר לבש' create a היקש between taking off and putting on. Each one needs its own קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And אהרן shall come to the אהל מועד and take off the linen garments that he put on.' Why does it say 'that he put on'? Does a person take off anything other than what he put on? Rather, it compares taking off to putting on. Just as putting on needs קידוש, so too taking off needs קידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the objection with an extra phrase in the פסוק. It shows that there must be two קידושין, one for taking off and one for putting on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אשר לבש' seem unnecessary, since you only take off what you put on. So the תורה is using them to link taking off with putting on. Putting on needs קידוש, so taking off needs one too, which gives two קידושין for every change.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this? (points to extra words)
Is it possible…? (shows the words seem obvious)
To compare two things through a היקש, so they share the same law
Taking off the garments
Putting on the garments

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for exactly two קידושין for every טבילה, which gives the total of ten קידושין on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And Aaron shall come into the Tent of Meeting

phrases.aramaic: וּפָשַׁט אֶת בִּגְדֵי הַבָּד אֲשֶׁר לָבַשׁ״,
phrases.english: and he shall remove the linen garments that he put on,"
Why does the verse say "that he put on"?

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם אָדָם פּוֹשֵׁט אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁלָּבַשׁ!
phrases.english: Does a person remove anything other than what he put on!
phrases.notes: He's not really asking. He's pointing out that the words seem extra.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to compare removing to donning:
just as donning requires sanctification,
so too removing requires sanctification.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וּבָא אַהֲרֹן אֶל אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וּפָשַׁט אֶת בִּגְדֵי הַבָּד אֲשֶׁר לָבַשׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 15 with a היקש from extra words in the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new source from extra words (היקש) that fills the gap left by the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר alone would give only one קידוש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Taking off is compared to putting on, so each one needs a קידוש. That makes two קידושין for every change.
steps.whatToRemember: Two קידושין per טבילה: one when taking off the old clothes and one when putting on the new ones, learned from the extra words 'אשר לבש'.

steps.title: רבי יהודה asks for the source of five immersions and ten sanctifications
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה asks where we learn that the כהן גדול does five טבילות and ten קידושין on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: From where do we learn the five טבילות and ten קידושין that the כהן גדול does on that day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and re-quotes רבי יהודה's ברייתא from step 7 so it can examine it closely. This line sets up the פסוק in the next step and the question that follows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's question and source already appeared in step 7. The גמרא repeats them here so it can check whether his פסוק really covers every change of clothes during the day.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asks for a source)
Five immersions and ten washings of hands and feet

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
From where are the five immersions and ten sanctifications

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁטּוֹבֵל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם?
phrases.english: that the High Priest immerses and sanctifies on that day?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מִנַּיִן לְחָמֵשׁ טְבִילוֹת וַעֲשָׂרָה קִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יהודה's ברייתא, first quoted in step 7, in order to examine it. Step 19 then points out a gap in it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that requires five טבילות and ten קידושין on יום כיפור

steps.title: Changing from one service to another requires immersion
steps.stepSummary: From 'ורחץ את בשרו במים במקום קדוש' we learn that whoever switches from one עבודה to another needs a טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And אהרן shall come to the אהל מועד… and wash his flesh in water in a holy place.' This teaches you that anyone who switches from one עבודה to another needs a טבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers his question with the פסוק. Right after taking off the white clothes, the כהן גדול must wash his body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places the washing of the body between taking off the white clothes and starting the next עבודה. From this, רבי יהודה builds a general rule: every switch between עבודות of different kinds needs a טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall wash his flesh (immersing the whole body)
From this you have learned
One who switches from one service to another (inner and outer)
Immersion of the whole body in a מקוה

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וּבָא אַהֲרֹן אֶל אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד
phrases.english: The verse says: "And Aaron shall come into the Tent of Meeting

phrases.aramaic: וְרָחַץ אֶת בְּשָׂרוֹ בַמַּיִם בְּמָקוֹם קָדוֹשׁ״,
phrases.english: and he shall wash his flesh in water in a holy place,"
phrases.notes: The two quoted parts come from ויקרא טז:כג and טז:כד.

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָמַדְתָּ שֶׁכׇּל הַמְשַׁנֶּה מֵעֲבוֹדָה לַעֲבוֹדָה —
phrases.english: from this you have learned that anyone who switches from service to service
requires immersion.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וּבָא אַהֲרֹן אֶל אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וְרָחַץ אֶת בְּשָׂרוֹ בַמַּיִם בְּמָקוֹם קָדוֹשׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to רבי יהודה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק requires washing the body after taking off the white clothes. This teaches a general rule that every switch between עבודות needs a טבילה.

steps.title: What about switching from gold back to white?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק only covers switching from white clothes to gold clothes. The גמרא asks for a source for switching from gold to white.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source for switching from white clothes to gold clothes. From where do we learn it for switching from gold clothes to white clothes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a gap in רבי יהודה's source. The search for a source for the opposite direction continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about taking off the linen (white) clothes and then washing before the next עבודה in gold clothes. So it directly proves only the white-to-gold change. The gold-to-white change still needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for one case)
White (linen) garments, worn for the inner עבודה
Gold garments, worn for the outer עבודה

phrases.english: We have found from white garments to golden garments;
from golden garments to white garments, from where?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן מִבִּגְדֵי לָבָן לְבִגְדֵי זָהָב, מִבִּגְדֵי זָהָב לְבִגְדֵי לָבָן מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the source in step 18 covers only one direction of change.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that switching from gold clothes to white clothes also needs a טבילה
